setup: Set the seat so the pad sits under your armpits
Backs of your arms flat on the pad
Feet flat, chest against the top of the pad
execution: Curl the bar up toward your shoulders
Keep your upper arms on the pad
Lower slowly until your arms are nearly straight
faults: Don't lift your elbows off the pad
Don't drop fast into the bottom
Don't lean back to swing the bar up

notes: The bottom is where the elbows are most exposed. Lower slowly, and stop just short of locking out if that feels better.
Pick a weight you can lower under control; heavy, fast reps that bounce at the bottom are the usual way this goes wrong.
Log the total including the bar. EZ bars and straight bars weigh different amounts.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at seated shoulder height, figure facing right, seated at a preacher bench with the arm pad angled about 45° down and away. Upper arms lie along the pad.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Seated, armpits at the top of the pad, upper arms along it. Arms nearly straight down the slope, underhand grip on the EZ bar, wrists straight.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Bar curled up toward the shoulders until the forearms are about vertical. Upper arms still flat on the pad; torso unchanged.

ikHints: Upper arms fixed on the pad in every frame
Torso and seat fixed; only the forearms move
guideBrief.barPath: An arc around the elbows, from low on the pad up toward the shoulders
emphasise: Upper arms stay on the pad
doNotShow: Fast drop or bounce at the bottom
